name: Persona
tagline: Realtime character presence for desktop voice experiences
description: Persona is a cross-platform desktop application that gives voice conversations an expressive visual identity: a VRM character rendered in a borderless window that animates idle and speaking motion in sync with the audio of a chosen playback process. It captures voice output through PipeWire on Linux, WASAPI process-loopback on Windows, or a Core Audio process tap on macOS, and never captures the microphone, saves audio, or sends anything over the network. A local MCP server exposes the character's animation controls, so AI coding agents like Codex can play installed animations and show or hide the window. Models and clips are managed through a catalog with packaged defaults and user-level overrides, and Persona ships as AppImage/DEB, NSIS installer, and macOS DMG/ZIP.
highlights: Cross-platform desktop character for Linux, Windows, and macOS 14.2+
Process-scoped voice-output capture via PipeWire, WASAPI loopback, or Core Audio tap
VRM/VRMA character library with packaged idle and speaking animations and custom actions
Local MCP server lets agents like Codex trigger animations and window controls
Privacy-first: no microphone capture, no audio recording, no network audio
curatorNote: Voice AI has been all ears and no face; Persona is one of the few projects giving a local voice assistant a real visual presence without sending audio anywhere. The MCP integration is a smart, agent-native way to let coding tools drive the character.
